title: Room Rate and Occupancy Charging on a Hotel Folio
content:
This ruling governs what is charged for the room and for those occupying it on a reservation in the Hotel Rate Plans range.

**A clause no longer in force.** The clause of this ruling reading "The room rate is posted night by night and room by room, at the rate the plan was sold at, and a rate once sold is never re-priced because the property's published rate has moved" is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis on which the room charge for the last night of a stay is worked out. The remaining clauses below stand as clauses in force.

**Occupants beyond the standard occupancy.** An occupant beyond the rate plan's standard occupancy is charged the plan's extra-adult or extra-child amount for every night they stay, counted per room. The charge for an extra adult is accordingly the plan's extra-adult amount per night multiplied by the nights stayed.

**Beds and board.** A cot or a rollaway bed is charged per night at the plan's amount, and a plan whose amount is zero provides it free; a plan that includes breakfast includes it for the declared occupants only.

**Arrival and departure outside the standard times.** Arrival before the property's standard check-in time and departure after its standard checkout time each carry the plan's own charge, except where the plan guarantees late departure, in which case nothing is charged.

**Upgrades.** A room upgrade accepted at check-in is charged per night at the plan's upgrade amount and never converts the reservation to the upgraded room type's own rate plan.

**Pets.** A pet is accepted only within the plan's weight limit and is charged once for the whole stay.

*Hypothetical arithmetic.* One extra adult on a plan whose extra-adult amount is 30.00 USD, staying three nights in one room, is charged 90.00 USD: the amount per night multiplied by the nights stayed, counted for that room alone.

superseded_clauses: The room rate is posted night by night and room by room, at the rate the plan was sold at, and a rate once sold is never re-priced because the property's published rate has moved.
